note: Verified against legislation.nsw.gov.au on 2026-08-14. Time limits for particular divisions and decision types sit in the enabling legislation, which displaces the general rule (r 25(4)(a)); a 14-day period applies to internal appeals against decisions in residential proceedings (r 25(4)(b)).

computation_provisions.summary: Reckoning of time: a period dating from a day, act or event excludes that day (s 36(1)); where the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public or bank holiday in the place where the thing is to be done, it may be done on the first following day that is not such a day (s 36(2)); extension powers survive expiry (s 36(3)).

period_rules.label: Internal appeal to the NCAT Appeal Panel (general period)
period_rules.citation: Civil and Administrative Tribunal Rules 2014 (NSW) r 25(4)(c)
period_rules.trigger: The later of notification of the decision and the day reasons are first given, orally or in writing (r 25(4)(c), r 25(4A))
warnings: A 14-day period applies to an internal appeal against a decision made in residential proceedings (r 25(4)(b)), and any period specified by the enabling legislation displaces this rule (r 25(4)(a)).
The Tribunal may extend time under s 41 of the Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 2013 (NSW).
